title: no task is dispatched on an unverified spec: a recorded spec preflight checks every acceptance line against the code and scope, and any rule-changing task must say what happens to work already in flight
acceptance:
Why. On 2026-10-04 about half of all rejected or blocked rounds came from specs firstmate wrote without checking them against the code:
- T-183: an id format the shared grammar rejects, a card shape fm-decide.sh refuses, and the grammar put in a file that one path does not load
- T-125: a vendored dependency left out, and a fixture path that had moved
- T-171: no migration for pins already written, which froze T-182, T-183 and T-125
Other changes invalidated work in flight with no plan for it: T-176's new lint hit T-178, and T-171 hit three tasks' pins. The captain asked for the rules themselves to be fixed so this cannot recur ("不是寫進記憶，是修正規則").

Spec preflight. `bin/fm-review.sh --spec-preflight --task <T> --spec <file>` runs one isolated, read-only crew round in the reviewer's sandbox and prompt discipline, on the current base. It checks every acceptance line against the code:
- (1) it is achievable within the declared scope, naming any file outside the scope that it needs
- (2) every caller, mirror, fixture and existing test the change touches is listed or covered (the class of bin/fm-*.sh, bin/lib/*, tests/** greps)
- (3) ids, formats, paths and interfaces the spec names exist and match the code
- (4) if the task changes a validation rule, lint, gate, schema or stored-record format, the spec states what happens to records and tasks already in flight (migration), and a test covers it
It ends with SPEC-OK:<task> or SPEC-GAPS:<task> and a numbered list, and the result is recorded as local evidence bound to the spec's SHA-256 (the same store as briefs and verdicts).

Enforcement. A task's first worker round refuses to start, exit 65 with the reason, unless a SPEC-OK record exists for exactly the spec bytes being pinned. A later spec change (repin) needs a new SPEC-OK for the new bytes. A SPEC-GAPS result is shown to firstmate, who amends the spec and preflights again. The refusal names the command to run.

Rules in the skills. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md requires the preflight before every dispatch and every repin, and requires the migration clause for rule-changing tasks. It records that a SPEC-GAPS item cannot be waved through without amending the spec. skills/reviewer/SKILL.md makes a missing or untested migration for a rule-changing diff a REJECT finding.

Tests (fail first, stubs answering like the real vendors and tools, HERDR_ENV=0 in helpers):
- a first round without SPEC-OK is refused
- SPEC-OK for other bytes is refused
- SPEC-OK for the exact bytes starts the round
- a repin without a new SPEC-OK is refused
- the preflight prompt contains the four checks and the closing markers
Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Workers do not run the suites.

Scope widened by captain decision D-firstmate-workflow-T185-2 (A, 2026-10-04): bin/fm-herdr.py carries an explicitly bound spec-preflight mode in the managed invocation, its role context, completion classification (SPEC-OK/SPEC-GAPS) and the authenticated final selector; ordinary reviewer markers and authentication are unchanged.

Scope widened by captain decision D-firstmate-workflow-T185-3 (A, 2026-10-04): bin/fm-canary.sh records a SPEC-OK, marked as a canary fixture, for the exact bytes of each fixture spec it writes before starting a worker round, so the drill runs under the new refusal without any exemption in fm-worker.sh.
